_comment: Audit queries needed to statistically distinguish a genuine model from a substituted one, as a function of the per-query accuracy gap Δ between them. Sample size from the standard two-proportion test: n ≈ K/Δ², K = (z_{1-α/2}+z_power)²·2·p̄·(1−p̄), at 80% power (z_power=0.8416) and a benchmark baseline accuracy p̄=0.6 for the variance term. Δ values are measured accuracy gaps from published quantization/substitution benchmarks (see sources). n is queries per arm; auditing also needs a reference run, so total work is ~2n.

substitutions.label: FP4 (well-calibrated)
substitutions.note: 90.8% → 90.7%; a tuned 4-bit cast that barely moves the score

substitutions.label: FP8
substitutions.note: 70.24% → 69.64% (−0.6 pt); identical on HumanEval — the default cheap endpoint

substitutions.label: INT8 (GPTQ, code probe)
substitutions.note: 39.02% → 37.20% (−1.8 pt) on code, but lossless on reasoning

substitutions.label: INT4 (GPTQ/AWQ)
substitutions.note: a 7.8-pt MMLU drop; visible but still needs hundreds of probes

substitutions.label: Smaller model (70B → 8B)
substitutions.note: ≈82% → ≈68%; swap the whole model and the gap is wide
